name: Czech nationalism
summary: Czech nationalism holds the Czechs to be a nation defined by language, history and culture, entitled to cultural survival and self-government. It grew out of the 19th-century National Revival against Germanisation, sought equality of nations inside the Habsburg state, then independence in 1918 and again in 1993. Today it is found across the party spectrum, with a sovereigntist, anti-immigration strand led by Freedom and Direct Democracy.
scope: The mainstream Czech national movement from the National Revival (Jungmann, Palacký, 1848 Old Czech programme) through the 1918 independence movement (Masaryk, Kramář) to the postwar nation-state and the modern sovereigntist strand (SPD). Czechoslovakism is covered by its own profile. Economic positions are mostly indifferent, since parties from Svobodní to the Communists claim the label, so most economic answers are low confidence.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Inferred: Czech national movements since the Revival backed an inclusive national community, and Czech parties across the spectrum accept public health insurance; the sources do not address it.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Inferred: the sources do not discuss wages, and both left and right nationalist parties listed in the article hold differing economic lines.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The article lists both Svobodní and the Communists as nationalist parties, so the national ideology itself has no economic line.

public-ownership.rationale: Nationalism is attached to parties from KSCM to ODS, so adherents split on public ownership.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: The national program does not decide tax levels; the parties listed range from free-market to Communist.

unions-good.rationale: Czech nationalism is a cross-class movement that treats unions neither as central nor as an enemy, and parties differ.

property-fundamental.rationale: Inferred: the movement drew on a bourgeois, small-property national society, but sources give no direct statement on property.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Left and right nationalist parties disagree on regulation, and the Revival and Palacký sources say nothing on it.

cut-welfare.rationale: Inferred: SPD-style nationalism criticizes benefit abuse but older Czech nationalism backed national solidarity; weak lean against cutting.

worker-ownership.rationale: Inferred: Czech nationalism is a cross-class national project, not a worker-ownership program, though left nationalist parties exist.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Security-minded nationalists accept surveillance against terrorism, while direct-democracy and liberal strands resist, so they split.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Inferred: national-conservative strands lean against legalization, while liberal strands favour it; weak lean from the SPD program.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: The SPD resists speech limits regarding Islam while mainstream nationalists accept ordinary hate-speech laws; a split.

strong-leader.rationale: Inferred: Palacký and the liberal Revival worked through assemblies and federal constitutions, though direct-democracy parties favour referendums over strongmen.

state-harmful.rationale: Czech nationalism seeks its own state or autonomous kingdom (Palacký sought a Czech kingdom of Bohemia, Moravia and Silesia), so it treats the state as necessary.

limit-guns.rationale: Not a national question; Czech gun culture is relaxed, yet no nationalist source takes a side.

empower-police-military.rationale: National-conservative strands such as the SPD stress order and sovereignty while liberal nationalists do not, so adherents split.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Inferred from conservative national strands; the sources do not discuss it.

decide-locally.rationale: Palacký wanted Bohemian autonomy from Vienna but a unified Czech-lands kingdom, a split between regional autonomy and a nation-wide state.

rehabilitation.rationale: The national program does not touch penal philosophy; adherents range from rehabilitation-minded liberals to law-and-order conservatives.

traditional-family.rationale: Inferred from the national-conservative SPD program, which resists same-sex civil weddings; older movements gave little attention.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: The SPD strongly opposes civil weddings for same-sex couples, though the Czech mainstream is more mixed.

abortion-legal.rationale: Czech society is among the most secular in Europe and abortion has been legal since the 1950s, so mainstream adherents accept legality; inferred.

more-religion-public.rationale: The Revival was Hussite-minded and Protestant-sympathetic, and Czech society is notably secular, so a larger public role for religion is not a nationalist goal.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Inferred: Czech nationalism does not frame history through race; modern strands reject quota-style correction.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Inferred from national-conservative strands; the sources do not address it.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The Revival's stated aim was to resurrect the Czech language, culture and identity against Germanisation, which makes cultural preservation the core of the ideology.

gradual-change.rationale: Palacký sought constitutional change inside Austria while Masaryk and Kramář pursued independence by revolution in 1918, so adherents split.

reduce-immigration.rationale: The SPD, the main modern nationalist party, strongly opposes illegal immigration and EU quotas and wants stricter rules, though other nationalist parties are milder.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Modern Czech nationalism stresses national sovereignty and the SPD seeks EU exit; earlier nationalists preferred protection by a multinational state.

free-trade.rationale: The article ties Czech economic nationalism only to the 1990-92 Slovak subsidy grievance; no trade line is attached to the nation.

nation-first.rationale: SPD and sovereigntist strands put national sovereignty first, while liberal nationalism is more internationalist; majority lean positive.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: A small-nation outlook sympathises with protecting peoples, but nationalists distrust foreign wars; split.

open-borders.rationale: Modern Czech nationalism rejects open borders and multiculturalism; the national community is defined by shared culture and language.

limit-growth.rationale: Not addressed; no sources tie Czech nationalism to degrowth.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Inferred: sovereigntist nationalist parties are sceptical of costly EU climate mandates; weak.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Czech nationalism is indifferent to technological optimism; it is a cultural and political movement.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Inferred: Czech parties of all kinds back nuclear energy as a national resource; sources do not state it.

revolution-justified.rationale: Palacký worked through constitutional channels, yet the 1918 break with Austria-Hungary was revolutionary; split.

experts-over-public.rationale: Direct-democracy nationalist parties distrust expert rule, but older Revival elites were scholars; weak lean.

central-planning.rationale: Left nationalist parties exist, but the movement's core is national, not planning; weak lean against.

socialized-markets.rationale: Not a national question; left and right nationalist parties would answer differently.

land-value-tax.rationale: A fiscal-design idea that the movement does not address.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Not a national question; parties on the nationalist list differ.

basic-income.rationale: Inferred: nationalist parties stress work and benefit limits; sources silent.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Czech nationalists are split between economic nationalists and free-market parties like Svobodní.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The left nationalist parties in the article favour it, the right ones do not; split.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Inferred: the Revival drew on rural and small-holder Czech life as the authentic nation, but no program on property was found.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Czech nationalism takes the nation, not abolition of classes, as its unit; even left nationalist parties in the article do not seek it.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Not addressed; Svobodní aside, nationalist parties do not call for it.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: State-recognised wage bodies are a corporatist model that Czech nationalism, working through parliament and parties, never adopted.

one-party-rule.rationale: Palacký sought constitutional rights and equality of nations; Czech nationalism in 1918 built a parliamentary state.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Palacký backed a Czech kingdom within the Habsburg realm, while 1918 nationalism founded a republic, so adherents split.

democracy-best.rationale: Mainstream Czech nationalism since 1918 stood for parliamentary democracy and the movement's modern parties accept it, though some distrust elites.

direct-votes.rationale: The SPD's program centres on direct democracy and referendums, though not all nationalists share it.

workers-councils.rationale: Councils were never a nationalist form; Czech nationalism works through national parliaments.

right-to-secede.rationale: Palacký proclaimed the secession of the Czech nation from German history and the movement sought independence from Austria-Hungary; the 1993 split also happened peacefully.

natural-rulers.rationale: Palacký wrote that nature knows neither dominant nor yoked nations, a claim of equal standing.

political-violence-never.rationale: Revivalists were non-violent, yet the movement later endorsed wartime resistance and postwar expulsions as legitimate; split.

war-builds-character.rationale: Palacký's small-nation outlook sought security through legal equality; no source ties Czech nationalism to war as a virtue.

separate-church-state.rationale: Czech society is notably secular and the Revival revived Hussite memory against Catholic Habsburg re-Catholicisation; mild lean to separation.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Revival Hussite heritage and Czech secularism make scripture-based law foreign to the movement.

private-courts-defense.rationale: The movement seeks a national state, so private defence is unrelated and opposed.

military-superiority.rationale: Small-nation Czech outlook prizes collective security, not superiority; inferred.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The ideology holds Czechs to be a nation with cultural unity, and the postwar settlement aimed at a nation-state, but the 1918 state was multinational; lean positive.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Czech nationalism takes the nation, not class, as the basic unit of history, even on its left wing.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Left nationalist parties exist, but no source supports it as a national position; weak lean against.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: No Czech claim applies; the question is outside the national concern.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Inferred: Czechs had no overseas empire and the issue is not part of the movement.

civilizational-union.rationale: Palacký favoured a Danubian union of nations under law, not a union on civilizational lines; the movement is nation-state oriented.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Nationalism asks loyalty to the nation, yet free-market nationalists endorse self-interest; split.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Palacký grounded politics in the rights of nations, so rights come first.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: The Revival romanticised the Czech landscape and countryside, but no source states a view on nature's intrinsic worth.

limit-population.rationale: A nationalist concern with national survival leans against population limits; inferred.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Inferred: Czech nationalism treats industrialized Czech lands as a source of pride.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Czech nationalism is indifferent to technological acceleration.

human-enhancement.rationale: Not addressed by the national movement and parties are split.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Direct-democracy and sovereigntist strands want citizens, not algorithms, to decide; inferred.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: No national position; security and civil-liberty nationalists split.

restore-past-order.rationale: The Revival looked back to the medieval kingdom and Kralice language yet built a modern nation; split.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Pragmatism is a common claim of ANO-type parties in the list, but the national ideology is not committed.

direct-action.rationale: The movement worked through assemblies and parties; weak lean against.

means-match-ends.rationale: No national position on this ethical claim.

return-to-foraging.rationale: The Revival celebrated rural life but aimed at a modern literate nation, not a hunter-gatherer past.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: A Marxist utopian goal; Czech nationalism, even in its left wing, does not seek it.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Left nationalist parties may accept it as an ideal, but the national movement as such does not make it a goal.

production-for-use.rationale: Inferred: outside the national program, though the Communist party sits in the article's nationalist list.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Inferred: the movement does not use a class-exploitation framing.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Nationalism centres on the nation; even Communist parties in the nationalist list do not rest on this thesis.

collective-farming.rationale: The Revival idealised independent rural life; collectivisation is not part of it.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Not a nationalist thesis; the movement sees conflict as between nations such as Czechs and Germans.

taxation-theft.rationale: Czech nationalism builds a national state; libertarian parties are a small minority.

harm-principle.rationale: Palacký's liberalism fits, but national-conservative strands favour moral limits as well; split.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Palacký grounded claims in the rights of nations, so group rights are central.

conscription.rationale: Czech nationalism saw the national army as essential, yet the Czech Republic abolished conscription in 2004 with wide consensus.

exit-over-voice.rationale: A nationalist movement values voice and a rooted national community rather than exit.

state-as-business.rationale: ANO-type parties favour business-style government but nationalism treats the state as a national community; weak lean.

positive-liberty.rationale: The national movement has no line; left nationalists accept it and free-market nationalists do not.

media-academia-power.rationale: Populist strands claim media power, but the Revival was led by scholars and writers; split.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Czech nationalism defines the nation by language and culture rather than race.

organic-representation.rationale: Not addressed; Czech nationalism worked through parliaments and parties.

total-state.rationale: Palacký sought rights and autonomy, not a state directing all life.

national-rebirth.rationale: The Czech National Revival is itself a national rebirth from German dominance, though without the radical decadence myth.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Czech nationalism claims a historic Bohemian territory and Palacký stressed small-nation security; no expansionist program.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Not a feudal doctrine; modern nationalism rests on the nation.

bound-labor.rationale: The Revival was a movement of the emancipated peasants and townspeople, so serfdom was left behind.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Palacký's History of the Czech Nation claimed scholarly truth against German historians, implying neutral knowledge is attainable.

universal-morality.rationale: Nationalism stresses national particularity, yet Palacký invoked natural rights; split.

single-common-good.rationale: The nation as common good fits, but party pluralism is accepted; split.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: The national movement takes no line, though Czech governments are strongly pro-Israel; adherents differ.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: No Czech national program on diaspora return; split.

revive-national-language.rationale: The Revival's central work was reviving Czech as a language of administration, schools and the intelligentsia, with Jungmann's dictionary shaping it.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Left nationalists would back it and right ones not; split.

school-vouchers.rationale: No national position; free-market nationalists support it and others do not.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Fiscal conservatism versus left economics divide nationalist parties.

economic-freedom.rationale: Svobodní accept the link; Communist nationalists do not; split.

rule-by-example.rationale: Czech national politics rests on laws and parliament, not rulers' personal example.

national-self-determination.rationale: Palacký wrote that the rights of nations are the rights of Nature and demanded equality for the Czech language and nation, the core of the doctrine.

force-without-un.rationale: Sovereigntists reject UN authority, but Czech nationalists also dislike foreign wars; split.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Czech tradition is secular and rationalist, but the sources do not state it for nationalism.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: The SPD and other nationalists want benefits limited to citizens.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Inferred from nationalist-right parties that campaign against benefit abuse.

class-collaboration.rationale: Czech nationalism treats nation as the shared unit across classes; the Revival was cross-class.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: The Revival was precisely about recovering inherited cultural institutions like the National Museum and Matice česká.

dominated-front.rationale: Palacký rejected Russian universal monarchy and sought protection of small nations inside a legal Danubian union, so a bloc of dominated countries against the West is not a Czech nationalist idea.

workers-nation.rationale: Left nationalist parties accept national lines but the core is nation first.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Palacký's equal rights language and 1918 democratic tradition lean against law fixing gender roles, though conservatives differ.

ban-interest.rationale: Not part of any Czech national program.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Czech nationalism defines nation by language and culture, with no race-segregation law in the Czech tradition.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The movement frames the state as national, not class, institution.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Inferred from sovereigntist parties' opposition to EU green policy.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: The SPD rejects multiculturalism and expects cultural adaptation.

elite-replacement.rationale: SPD rhetoric warns of Islamisation but a deliberate-replacement plot is not a mainstream Czech nationalist tenet; split.

proportional-representation.rationale: The Czech Republic uses PR; the national ideology has no line and parties differ.

national-mission.rationale: Palacký's small-nation view sought protection of nations, not export of a system.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: National-conservative strands reject the thesis, while liberal nationalists accept parts; weak lean.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: SPD and ANO-type nationalist parties campaign on anti-elite populism.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Palacký's equality principle makes eugenic limits contrary to the movement.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Czech nationalists defend the postwar decrees against prosecution while 1989 accountability is accepted; split.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Czech nationalism asks a national state to defend language and culture.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Czech nationalism is not racial, and the sources do not tie to it.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Palacký rested the case on equal rights for all nationalities and religions.

socialism-one-country.rationale: A Marxist debate outside the national movement.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: No national position; Czech nationalism has no overseas settlement.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Inferred: citizens equal before law, a general liberal view.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Hussite-minded, secular Czech culture does not restrict conversion.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: A South Asian religious-political demand with no place in Czech tradition.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Czech society is secular and state schools do not teach religion as standard; inferred.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist doctrine outside the national movement.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Palacký grounded Czech claims in the rights of nations and constitutional freedom, implying consent.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilist nationalists would agree; liberal ones would not; split.

population-transfer.rationale: The Czech mainstream, with Beneš, justified expelling the Sudeten Germans after 1945 and still defends the decrees, though many now regret it.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: A strict libertarian principle, whereas Czech nationalism accepted the force of the postwar expulsions.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Czech nationalism saw a centuries-long Czech-German struggle in Bohemia, but did not make competition a theory of progress.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Inferred: Czech state banned parties in the past, sources silent.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Palacký rejected domination, writing that nature knows neither dominant nor yoked nations.

separated-powers.rationale: Inferred from the liberal-constitutional demands of the 1848 Czech movement.

vanguard-party.rationale: A Leninist doctrine; the Communist party in the nationalist list is the only adherent.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Left nationalists accept and right ones do not; split.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: A UK policy with no Czech national position.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: No national position on labour law; split by left versus right.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Not a Czech nationalist claim; adherents locate causes in institutions or history.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: SPD rejects multiculturalism, and Czech nationalism treats cultural unity as its aim.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Direct-democracy strands favour referendums, not lotteries; weak lean against.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Inferred from Palacký's constitutional rights stance, though security-minded nationalists accept emergencies.

party-controls-media.rationale: Inconsistent with the movement's constitutional rights tradition.

party-commands-army.rationale: Only the Communist party among nationalist parties supported such control historically, and the national movement as such does not.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Inferred from the SPD's stricter immigration rules.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Populist strands might favour it; no national line.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: No national position on party organisation.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: The SPD seeks exit from the EU and parties like Přísaha and Tricolour are Eurosceptic, though ODS-type nationalists accept membership; majority lean against.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Czech nationalism built a parliamentary republic in 1918 where the president is not the executive commander.

church-by-bishops.rationale: The Revival's Hussite memory is anti-hierarchical, and Czech Catholic nationalism is a small strand.

clerical-rule.rationale: The Hussite-minded, secular tradition of Czech nationalism rejects clerical rule.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Czech nationalism is patriotic; Masaryk and Kramář worked for independence, not defeatism.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Revivalist Czech literature depended on freedom from Habsburg censorship; inferred.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: The Czech president has a two-term limit and nationalists have not contested it.

recall-officials.rationale: The SPD's direct-democracy program favours citizen control, so recall fits.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: SPD questions NATO commitments yet Czech governments back the alliance; weak lean against.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Not part of any Czech national program.

people-in-arms.rationale: The Czech nation-state relies on a professional army; no national call for a militia.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Revival writers like Erben and Němcová treated rural life as the authentic Bohemia.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Czech nationalism has no divided-nation question after 1993; Slovaks are a separate nation.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Populist strands say so, yet the Revival was led by scholars; split.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Modern nationalists defend Judeo-Christian values against Islam, though the Revival asserted equality of nations; split.

death-penalty.rationale: Czech opinion is divided and the Czech state abolished it in 1990; adherents split.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: National conservatives dislike it, liberal nationalists accept it; split.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: The secular, scholarly Czech tradition does not back creationism; inferred.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Conservatives would restrict while liberal nationalists would not; split.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: The 1945 decrees gave citizenship by declared Czech or Slovak nationality, so ethnic criteria shaped the state; lean positive.

minority-language-support.rationale: The Revival fought for the Czech language against German dominance, though Czechoslovakia accepted minority rights; lean against.

religious-exemptions.rationale: The SPD resists accommodating Muslim practice, so exemptions for minorities are disfavoured.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: No national position on this Millian claim.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Left nationalists may favour; no national line.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Czech nationalism achieved independence in 1918 and 1993 without demanding economic transformation.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Inferred: 1848 and 1918 movements founded constitutions through national bodies.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: The Palacký tradition prizes constitutional freedoms; inferred.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: The Czech Republic has no nuclear weapons and nationalists have not asked for them.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Czechia introduced direct presidential election in 2013 and direct-democracy nationalists support it.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Sovereigntists dislike ECB independence but ODS-type nationalists accept it; split.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Czech nationalists took an inflexible line on Sudeten return, but there is no general principle on conceding land; split.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: No national position; left and right differ.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: A Marxist-internal debate on which the movement has no stance.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Inferred from sovereigntist stance against EU environmental rules.

collective-defense.rationale: Czechs historically sought allied guarantees (1918 and Czechoslovakia in 1930s); inferred.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Czech nationalism rejected the 1938-39 annexations and Palacký stood for the integrity of Bohemian lands.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Hussite memory and Czech secularism favour civil control of churches; inferred.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Masaryk is honoured as a head of state above party, but the modern directly elected president is partisan; split.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: The 1993 Czech-Slovak split was peaceful, and nationalism holds self-determination valid.

region-keeps-system.rationale: A one-country-two-systems question with no Czech parallel.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Divine rulers are alien to the Revival and to Czech secular republicanism.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Right nationalist parties such as ODS favour; left do not; split.

character-from-environment.rationale: No national position on nature versus nurture.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Palacký demanded constitutional rights for nations and subjects, so an unbound ruler is rejected.

mixed-constitution.rationale: No national position on this classical theory.

leader-cult.rationale: The Czech tradition is not leader-centred, though Masaryk is honoured.

equal-parenting.rationale: No national position; conservatives and liberals split.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: A Maoist doctrine outside the national movement.

land-redistribution.rationale: The postwar decrees confiscated and redistributed German land, but land reform is not otherwise a national program; split.

refugee-return.rationale: The Czech mainstream rejects return of expelled Germans, upholding the Beneš decrees.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Czech nationalism claims historic Bohemian lands, not territory abroad.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Alien to the secular Czech culture.

women-must-cover.rationale: Modern nationalists oppose Islamic dress codes and Czech tradition has none.

common-currency.rationale: Czech Republic keeps the koruna, and nationalist parties oppose euro adoption.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: The movement is split between Slavic reciprocity and Czechoslovakism on one side and a sovereign Czech nation-state on the other; the 1993 split favoured separate states.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Palacký wanted national equality in a multinational state which fits this model, but Czech nationalism later denied it to Germans; split.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: No national position; Czech nationalism sought its own state but stayed in place.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Nationalism stresses language and identity, not material production, as the driver of history.

ban-cartels.rationale: Competition policy is not a national question.

no-bailouts.rationale: Free-market nationalists oppose bailouts, left ones accept; split.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Populists lean majoritarian while liberal nationalists defend courts; split.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: The nationalist right opposes quotas; weak lean.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: The Czech lands are a trading economy; autarky is no national goal.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Left nationalists favour, sovereigntists dislike; split.

moral-incentives.rationale: A Maoist and Guevarist idea outside the national movement.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: A foco theory that is not a Czech national tactic.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Czech nationalism built a republic in 1918 and the movement challenged Habsburg-aristocratic dominance.

history-own-civilization.rationale: The Revival promoted Czech history and language teaching; Palacký's history of the Czech nation is its core text.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Palacký rejected dominant nations, so civilizing rule by some peoples over others contradicts his stance.

patriotic-education.rationale: The Revival aimed to teach national identity and language in schools.

public-money-creation.rationale: Monetary reform is not a national question.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Czech nationalists define themselves against Habsburg Vienna and have no imperial nostalgia, but some value Central European ties; split.

delink-world-market.rationale: The Czech economy is deeply integrated; delinking is not nationalist policy.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: A Leninist thesis with no place in Czech nationalism.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Palacký's equal rights principle lean against; libertarian nationalists differ.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Inferred from Palacký's demand for constitutional equality of nations and religions.

elective-rulers.rationale: Palacký backed a Czech kingdom, 1918 nationalists chose a republic; split.

minority-veto.rationale: Czech nationalism seeks majority-nation rule with minority rights; a veto would obstruct it.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: The Revival invoked the Hussite tradition and Czech estates' rights against Habsburg centralism.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Palacký led the Bohemian Diet's nationalist-federal party; inferred.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: No national position; the Revival's leaders were mostly bourgeois.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: The Revival required active public engagement in language, scholarship and politics.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: A critical-theory claim; left nationalists may accept it, others do not.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: A Gramscian claim outside the national movement.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Dependency theory; left nationalists may agree, the rest do not.

native-born-offices.rationale: Inferred from the nationalist-right restricting immigration.

party-own-road.rationale: Czech nationalists resent foreign direction as such; inferred.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Not relevant to the Czech case.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Czech nationalists lost territory only in 1938; not a modern claim.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Left nationalists accept it as a founding value, right ones object; split.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Right-nationalist Czech parties stress the communist legacy; not directly sourced.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: An American question with no Czech national position.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Czech nationalists split over Soviet-era and German-era monuments.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Sovereigntists say each nation chooses its own institutions, but the Czech tradition aspired to Western ones; split.

military-guardian-role.rationale: The Czechoslovak army stayed under civilian control; no tradition of a guardian role.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Economic nationalists favour, liberal ones do not; split.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Czech divorce law is liberal and no national position exists; split.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Direct-democracy strands might accept; no national line.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Free-market nationalists favour, others do not; split.

land-use-tenure.rationale: The Revival romanticised independent peasant ownership, not usufruct tenure.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Inferred from the parliamentary constitutionalism of Palacký's Bohemian Diet politics.

single-official-language.rationale: The Revival insisted on Czech as the language of administration and schools, pushing out German, though the 1920 state also recognised minority languages.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Nationalists may support restrictions while EU membership forbids them; split.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: The nationalist right rejects outcome-based discrimination tests.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: A small state with no tradition of proxy warfare.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Czech nationalism treats the 1968 Warsaw Pact invasion as a violation of national sovereignty; inferred from the national principle.

corporate-influence.rationale: Populists condemn lobbying while ODS-type parties do not; split.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Sovereigntists favour, liberal nationalists do not; split.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Inferred from nationalist concern about the nation's survival.

job-guarantee.rationale: Left nationalists favour, others do not; split.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: The movement built and defended a national legal order.

non-intervention.rationale: Small-nation sympathy for sovereignty versus support for human rights; split.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Czech nationalism has not been centred on conspiracy, though SPD rhetoric targets Islam.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Conservatives oppose; liberal nationalists indifferent; weak lean against.

local-production.rationale: The Revival valued rural life, but no program favours local production.

informal-organisation.rationale: The national movement organised through societies such as Matice česká and parties.

national-law-over-international.rationale: SPD and sovereigntist strands put national constitution above EU and international bodies.

religious-nation.rationale: Czech national identity is defined by language and history, not religion, in a notably secular society.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Palacký opposed domination by great powers, whether German or Russian.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: The 1990-92 grievance that Czech lands subsidised Slovakia shows the impulse, but it concerned nations, not regions.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Even Czech left nationalists in the list accept private personal property.

defeat-communism.rationale: Right nationalists want it defeated, while the Communist party is on the nationalist list; split.

religion-illusion.rationale: The Revival's Hussite memory and Czech secularism, but nationalism does not teach this Marxist thesis.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Left nationalists accept, others do not; split.

socialized-care.rationale: Conservative nationalists favour family care; weak lean against.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Revivalists like Jungmann coined Czech words in place of German ones but borrowed from Slavic languages, so purism was selective.

majority-settlement.rationale: After 1945 Czech settlers were resettled into the former Sudeten borderlands, a state policy of majority settlement.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Palacký asserted Czech lands never belonged to the German nation and Czech claims to the Bohemian crown lands rest on history.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Not a Czech nationalist position; mainstream parties reject it.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Even the SPD opposes only same-sex civil weddings; Czechoslovakia decriminalised in 1962.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Contradicts the constitutional liberalism of Palacký and the 1918 republic.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Alien to the secular Czech culture shaped by the Hussite and Revival heritage.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Palacký wrote that nature knows neither dominant nor yoked nations.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Not applicable to secular Czech nationalism.

participatory-democracy.rationale: The SPD's direct-democracy program favours citizen participation.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: The nationalist right rejects the thesis.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Czech nationalism spans the left-right spectrum, which partly supports this claim, but parties still identify with sides.

alienated-labor.rationale: A Marxist concept outside the national movement.

islam-incompatible.rationale: The SPD argues migrant quotas will Islamise Europe and defends Judeo-Christian values.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Palacký grounded rights in nature and nations, not divine authority.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Anti-Muslim nationalists favour, others do not; split.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: The national movement has no line on workplace law, and the parties carrying the label range from liberal to nationalist-conservative.

social-market-economy.rationale: Czech parties across the spectrum accept; the national ideology has no line.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Czech nationalism keeps a national army.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Czechs joined NATO yet Euroscepticism flirts with neutrality; split.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Czech nationalism established a republic in 1918, so hereditary succession of a leader is not part of it.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: No national position; left nationalists favour, others do not.

property-franchise.rationale: The Czech movement demanded equal rights, and 1918 introduced universal suffrage.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Inferred: ecofeminist theory has no place in Czech nationalism, and the national-conservative strand in the SPD program is hostile to feminist frames.

reification.rationale: A Marxist critical-theory claim outside the national movement's concerns; left nationalist parties in the article may accept it, the rest ignore it.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Left nationalist parties such as KSCM accept the claim, while liberal and right nationalists reject it, so adherents split.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Inferred from the constitutional liberalism of Palacký's programme.

racial-franchise.rationale: Czech nationalism is not racial and 1918 introduced universal suffrage.

online-participation.rationale: Direct-democracy parties may favour; no national line.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Not Czech national program; although interwar economic nationalism did have such episodes.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Direct-democracy parties may favour; no national line.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Left nationalists accept while free-market ones do not; split.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Czechia allows it, and national conservatives are split.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Czech society is secular, but state promotion was a communist policy.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Foreign to a national statist movement.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Czechoslovakism denied power sharing, while the 1969 federation had it; split.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Czech nationalism has no tradition of replacing the welfare state with charity.

term-limits.rationale: Populist parties may favour; no national line.

vote-delegation.rationale: Direct-democracy parties may favour; no national line.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: No national position; Czech society is secular.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Palacký's principle of equal rights and Masaryk-era values favour shared authority; inferred.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Nationalist right strongly restricts non-citizens' political role.

rent-control.rationale: Left nationalists favour; right ones do not.

abolish-ip.rationale: The Revival's scholarly and literary work depended on authors' rights; weak lean against.

uniformed-youth.rationale: The Czech Sokol gymnastic movement was uniformed and national, but sources do not describe it, and modern adherents split.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Czech nationalists debated US radar bases, but no national line on nuclear weapons.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Sovereigntists tend to oppose foreign bases while NATO supporters accept them; split.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Left nationalists accept, free-market ones do not; split.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Pacifism of this absolute kind is not part of Czech nationalism.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Revivalists linked the nation to medieval Bohemia and Palacký's history of the Czech nation, but with the acknowledgement of a break after 1620.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: A feminist-theory claim not shared by nationalist strands.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Czech national memory honours Hus and the resistance dead; inferred.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Czech nationalism is a secular cultural movement, not a struggle of good and evil.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Not applicable; the Czech homeland has not been described as a diaspora centre.

culture-before-state.rationale: Czech nationalism followed a cultural, language and scholarly Revival long before it demanded independence.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: The Czech national movement historically competed economically with Germans, but a majority-ownership program is not stated; split.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Palacký demanded the unity of the Bohemian lands as one kingdom, and the Czech nation wanted its territory unified.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: A socialist-internal claim; left nationalists may accept.

second-chamber.rationale: The Czech Senate exists; no national line.

person-over-state.rationale: Palacký grounded rights of nations, yet liberals put the person first, so adherents split.

spiritual-nature.rationale: The Revival had a Protestant heritage, but secular modern adherents split.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Palacký sought Bohemian autonomy not revocable at will, yet Czech nationalism became centralist after 1918; split.

gm-crops.rationale: No national position; sovereigntists tend to oppose EU-imposed regimes.

dense-cities.rationale: The Revival romanticised rural life, but no national position.

racial-pride.rationale: No national position; Czech nationalism takes pride in nation, not race.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Palacký sought security through rights, not conquest; inferred.

language-defines-nation.rationale: The Revival's task was recovering Czech as the core of nationhood, and Palacký called himself a Czech of Slavonic blood.

communal-electorates.rationale: Czech nationalism seeks a single national electorate; not a Czech model.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: The 1938 Munich Agreement left lasting mistrust of great powers, but no active plot narrative is in the sources; split.

free-public-college.rationale: Czech public universities are tuition-free and the Revival valued education; inferred.

future-generations.rationale: The Revival's concern for handing a national heritage forward suggests sympathy; inferred.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Palacký's liberal outlook suggests sympathy but no program; split.

capital-controls.rationale: The Czech economy is open; nationalists do not favour controls.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Inferred: the nation-state claims a monopoly of force.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Patriotic movements expect soldiers to serve.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Right nationalists favour, left do not; split.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Czech nationalism built, not smashed, the state.

sacred-nation.rationale: The Revival treated the nation as the supreme cultural unit but secularly; not described as sacred.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Not relevant, as Czech public universities are free.

public-service-media.rationale: Czech public radio and TV exist and the Revival valued Czech-language media; inferred.

farm-price-support.rationale: The Revival idealised the peasantry, but no farm-price program appears in the sources.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Not applicable to the Czech Republic.

workers-own-party.rationale: No national position; the Communist list entry aside.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Czechoslovakism took Czech and Slovak as one language and Czech nationalism otherwise treats Czech across Bohemia and Moravia as one language; lean positive.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Law-and-order nationalists favour; others do not.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Language is the core of Czech nationalism and the SPD expects cultural adaptation of newcomers.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Parties from Svobodní to the Communists claim the Czech nationalist label, so the movement has no position on union rules.

voter-id.rationale: The sources do not address voter ID; the label spans the whole party spectrum, so adherents are split.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Inferred: Czech national memory leans on Hussite and Protestant history against a state-favoured church, and the movement is secular-minded; not directly documented.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: The movement's sovereigntist strand (SPD) stresses direct democracy while the mainstream stresses national self-government; adherents are split.

premarital-sex.rationale: Inferred from the broadly secular Czech society the movement operates in; the sources do not discuss sexual morality.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Inferred from the movement's civic, constitutional tradition and the SPD's direct-democracy emphasis; shutdowns are not discussed.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Economic positions are mostly indifferent across the parties claiming the label, and no source addresses cash-transfer design.

women-suffrage.rationale: Inferred from Masaryk-era nationalism and the 1918 republic, which gave women the vote; the sources I used do not state it.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Inferred: the movement's religious memory is of Hussite reform and not of oppression by religion; no stance is documented.

race-social-construct.rationale: Czech nationalism defines the nation by language, history and culture rather than race, but the sovereigntist strand is split on race questions; inferred.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; the label spans the party spectrum, so adherents are split.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Inferred: Czech nationalism is indifferent on economic doctrine, and the sources do not address first appropriation.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Inferred from Palacký's rights of nations and modern Czech parties' general acceptance of international law; the sources do not address criminal courts.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Inferred from Czech society's secular character and the Hussite and Protestant memory of the Revival, not from any stated position on inerrancy.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Inferred from Czech national movements' liberal, equality-of-nations tradition; the sources do not address gender in self-government.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Inferred from the postwar legacy of rejecting the communist regime and the modern nationalist strand's anti-communism; the sources do not address it directly.

indirect-election.rationale: Inferred from the modern nationalist party's push for direct democracy and referendums.

national-church-status.rationale: Inferred: the Hussite and Protestant memory is part of national identity, but modern Czech nationalism is secular and the sources show no church privilege.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Czech nationalists treated Sudeten German autonomy demands as a threat to the state, and the Beneš decrees expelled Germans rather than grant them autonomy.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Inferred from Palacký's emphasis on the rights of peoples and the modern nationalist party's support for direct democracy; plebiscites on territory are not discussed.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Inferred: Czech nationalism defended the historic borders of the Bohemian lands and later inherited borders, but colonial borders are not addressed.

simple-living.rationale: Inferred: the sources and parties across the spectrum give no common line on simple living.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Inferred: the sources do not address indigenous peoples, and a Czech nation-state view favours free settlement within the state.

equal-conscription.rationale: Inferred from the equality-of-nationalities and liberal tradition; the sources do not address conscription.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: The National Revival's romantic, rural and historical focus on land, language and Hussite memory expresses a bond with the homeland.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from Czech nationalism's rights-of-nations liberalism, Palacky's 1848 programme and the rule-of-law state.

close-ties-china.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the sovereigntist strand's Western and EU-centred debates and Czech Western orientation.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Inferred from the national-protection logic, though the sources document no policy for Czechs abroad.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Adherents split: parties from Svobodni to the Communists claim the label, so no common line on resource ownership.

self-ownership.rationale: Adherents split across the economic spectrum; no common position on self-ownership is documented.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Adherents split across the economic spectrum, so no common line on consumption taxes.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Inferred from the sovereigntist strand's focus on benefits for citizens and the broad welfare tradition.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: The main modern nationalist party campaigns for direct democracy, which sidesteps party mediation; inferred for the wider strand.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the movement's equality-of-nations principle and anti-establishment populism.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Inferred from the Revival's secular national identity and Hussite memory, which defined Czechness by language and culture rather than confession.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Inferred from the Revival's blend of modern national culture with older traditions and history.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the liberal national movement of Palacky and Masaryk.

national-resource-control.rationale: Inferred from the sovereigntist strand's emphasis on national control over decisions affecting the country.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Inferred: parties from Svobodní to the Communists claim the Czech national label, so adherents are split and the sources do not address it.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Inferred: no source links Czech nationalism to financial regulation, and economic views span the spectrum.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Inferred: the movement's concerns were language and national rights; the sources do not address racial advancement, and adherents differ.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Inferred: Revival figures appealed to national and historic rights against Habsburg rule, but the sources do not state a view on unjust law; the later Beneš decrees show legalism.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Anachronistic and economically indifferent: the sources do not address automation and adherents across the spectrum differ.

multipolar-world.rationale: Inferred: Palacký wanted Austria to shield small nations from German and Russian dominance, but modern sovereigntists (SPD) and Czech Atlanticists differ on the world order.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Inferred: the mainstream movement was liberal-national, not Marxist, though Communists also claimed the label; the sources do not discuss value theory.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Inferred: the Revival built a national community across classes and the movement included social-democratic and agrarian strands, but the sources do not state it.

material-over-identity.rationale: Anachronistic: Czech nationalism is itself an identity movement and the question concerns the modern left, so nothing is sourced.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Inferred: the mainstream movement was democratic and national, so rule by a communist party would be rejected, though the Communists claimed the label for part of the postwar period.

missingStatements.text: A people's language and culture deserve legal and educational protection against domination by a larger neighbouring nation.
missingStatements.rationale: The Revival and Palacký's 1848 demands centre on equality of the Czech language in public life against German dominance.

missingStatements.text: Small nations are best protected inside a larger multinational union that guarantees equal rights to every nationality.
missingStatements.rationale: Palacký's Frankfurt letter argued Austria must exist to protect the smaller peoples of central Europe from German and Russian absorption.
missingStatements.declined: Specific to Austro-Slavism; pool-sovereignty already asks the closest general question.

notes: Economic and social answers are low confidence because the label spans Communist, social-democratic, liberal and far-right parties. The sovereigntist SPD strand would answer more strongly on immigration, the EU and Islam than the classical Revival strand. Czech attitudes to the 1945 expulsions are contested.
